scenes.summary: You meet with Aleksandr who claims to be an agent of Erikssohn Trading House. He claims to know nothing about Hartmann and tells you that he might be a "scammer". Another agent named Hans who happens to be passing by also tells you how he became a recent victim. Before signing the contract, you decide to make a file of Agent Aleksandr.

lines.text: Greetings. You must be the Esteemed Endministrator of Endfield Industries. Pleased to meet you.
Someone else? No, Esteemed Endmin. I've been managing this contract since the very beginning.
My name is Aleksandr and I work at the business and sales department of ⟦key|Erikssohn Trading House⟧. This is my business card.
Esteemed Endmin, seeing your regal bearing and aura of leadership, I'm sure our deal will be successfully concluded today!
You don't look very enthusiastic. Please understand that this is a major contract — Is there anything you're concerned with?
Hartmann? I ... don't think I've heard about him before.
Wha? That actually happened?!
My Esteemed Endmin, fortunately you have observant eyes. That man is a scammer. Signing his bogus contract would be a mistake that cannot be salvaged!

You must have been too busy to keep yourself updated with the latest news. A notorious scammer recently made his way into Valley IV. He's now disguised as a corporate agent and has swindled plenty of honest businesses.
Think about it, Esteemed Endmin. The Endfield zipline suite has not been formally revealed to the market. Only agents most experienced in the transport business would sniff it out, right?
I'm not painting your product in a bad light... But zipline systems are marked with high initial costs. Everyone is cautious. Initial bids would tend to be more conservative.
Unless, of course, we're talking about ... a corporate spy who knows everyone else's bottom line. His bid would be too good to be true. His only aim is to get your signature on the bogus contract.

Anything like a verification key is a total fake. He might even create a shell company just to win your trust. And once you deliver the goods, he disappears with all your money and leaves you with nothing. You're lucky this hasn't happened to you.
Wait. Did you run into the scammer as well?
Ugh! I've heard plenty of stories about that scammer! People got scammed out of their goods and orders...

What's happening to our world? Business is tough enough already ... and now a fraud has decided to join the show! People are gonna hold onto their money. It'd be damn near impossible to make a proper deal...
Well met, good sir. I take it that you're in business and sales as well?
Heh. Just passing by, you know, just passing by... Heard you talking about the fraud so I had to give my two cents. Don't take my word for it, though.
So, my friend and ... my fellow negotiator. I'm Hans, and I'm trying to get some deals going as well. Seems fate has brought us all together. Here's my card. And here's one for you, too.
I represent a small business, and I really hope we don't have to deal with these scammers.
You see, Esteemed Endmin. I'm not the only one worried about scammers.
Now that we have a contract, I suppose we can have it formally signed at your office.
My name is Aleksandr and I work at the business and sales department of Erikssohn Trading House. This is my business card.

options: I thought I was meeting someone else.
Well met.
Did they scam you too?
I'm actually quite confused.
Roadside business negotiations are "great", I suppose.
Looks like I got left out of scammer-gate.
He was the company representative who met me yesterday.
There's no Hartmann in your company?
Hartmann is a fraud?
Did I meet a swindler?
Hold on. I need to update your file.
Where did Hartmann go?

scenes.summary: Hartmann rushes over to stop you. He and Aleksandr then mutually accuse each other as scammers. Hartmann shows you his company's handyterm to prove that Aleksandr is not on the list of Erikssohn employees.

lines.text: Endmin!!
I made it in time. DON'T SIGN THAT CONTRACT, ENDMIN!
Don't trust this guy, Endmin! He's no employee of ⟦key|Erikssohn⟧!
Well, well, Aleksandr. Top sales executive of a big company. Never expected you to steal my identity! How despicable!
Wait, what...?! He called me a scammer?!
Are you making fun of our Esteemed Endmin? I don't know you at all. You must be the scammer who crawled out from nowhere.
WHAT?! How dare you call me a scammer!
I'll show you... Look, Endmin! My leg still carries the wound from yesterday! A criminal cheat wouldn't let his leg get cut up like this, right?
Maybe you and your cronies did it for sympathy points.
Why you ... I ... I'm gonna...
Endmin! I have my company's handyterm right here. I'll show you our list of employees. Nobody in Erikssohn is called Aleksandr.

options: He told me you're a scammer.
Is this a joke to you guys?

r: He told me you're a scammer.
Is this a joke to you guys?

lines.text: Do you have any proof that I'm an identity thief?
We are civilized people, after all.

options: Submit List of Employees of Erikssohn Trading House.
I'll try to figure this out.

r: Submit List of Employees of Erikssohn Trading House.

scenes.summary: Aleksandr admits that he used some tricks and reveals that he is actually working for Clavis TGCC Trading. He then tells you that Erikssohn is doing very poorly and offers you a contract from Clavis, claiming that partnering with his company will be a wiser choice.

lines.text: Ugh. Fine. If things have come to this, playing this game no longer serves any purpose.
I'll just be honest with you, Endministrator. I did use a few business tricks to secure a meeting with you...
But this is part and parcel for anyone who wants to make the killer deal. Business can be cruel and merciless. Don't let this get to your head, Hartmann.
I'm treating you like family now, Endmin! Calling you our Esteemed Endministrator creates distance between us! Of course, I will maintain formalities if that is your wish!

I didn't plan to keep you in the dark, Esteemed Endmin. If things went my way, we would already be seated in your office going over the details of the deal — But Hartmann's sudden appearance interrupted my efforts.
My sudden appearance?! You're the criminal here, Aleksandr!
I might look like the bad guy now, Endministrator, but this isn't as simple as it looks. Perhaps you haven't heard about the situation at Erikssohn Trading House?
Endmin, I'm actually an agent representing ⟦key|Clavis TGCC Trading⟧.
Very observant, Endmin!
But that's no reason for you to dress up as an Erikssohn agent! Endmin, don't trust this Aleksandr! Tons of folk in the TGCC call him the Viper... And Clavis isn't as good as he describes.

Well, I must confess that I was desperate. I know the bid from Clavis won't get us into the final round, but I refuse to give up... Rest assured this is my personal doing and has nothing to do with my company.

Consider it my mistake for failing to secure more resources for this deal... But I see true potential in this product! That said, you should realize that it's quite revolutionary, and our market may not be ready to embrace it.
I've assured my higher-ups that this product will sell. But you know how slowly large companies move — they took too long to decide and missed the window to offer a better bid...
This is why I decided to approach you under a separate identity. The aim is to get me a chance to approach you about this new opportunity. I'm definitely not a scammer.
Well... Endmin...! Don't let this man mislead you! Erikssohn is small, but your product will be the star of our next season's catalog! Our finances are healthy enough to achieve the expected sales!
Really? I heard Erikssohn shut down several offices just last week.
And for your information, Endmin, Clavis has taken over the offices they closed.

Endmin, buying out the competition is Clavis's strategy! They even included it in their annual general meetings! I'm guessing Clavis is buying your zipline sales plan just to pave the way for their lousy counterfeit!
My company is completely committed to your zipline suite... It is Erikssohn's golden opportunity to open up a new market!
Every large company does that. Media coverage is designed to generate sensation and influence stock prices. These are just standard fluctuations. It's nothing to worry about.
Standard fluctuations? What about your recent massive layoffs? Are those standard too?
Well... Change brings about life. No one survives by sticking to the same old ways. This only proves that Clavis is a dynamic company!
Clavis is a name you can trust. In any case, we're far better than some financially distressed small-timer trying to cut off loose ends everywhere!
Why you... We're not financially distressed! We're just changing our corporate focus! A directional adjustment! That's all!
Well said. On behalf of Clavis TGCC Trading, I shall provide you with a new contract.

Clavis is far superior in terms of size, professionalism, and market share. We are way better than Erikssohn, a small-timer known for defaulting on their final payments. A contract with Clavis is definitely something you can trust!

Maybe we should wrap things up for now.

...I'm fine.

lines.text: Damn my luck... This isn't a major deal. Why is Aleksandr the Viper so interested in it...?
My wife just told me yesterday to read the horoscopes. The signs said today would be a day of "incredible success". I really thought everything would work out...
It's true, Endministrator... We do have some ... operational issues. This is why we're looking for new opportunities.
I never intended to hide it from you, I swear! I just don't want anything to ... significantly affect your judgment...

I've said everything I needed to say. I'm sure someone of your legendary acumen has carefully weighed every choice, and identified the option that benefits both parties. I have faith in your decision!
Clavis is one of the most reputable leaders in the transport and logistics sector of Talos-II. We have proven ourselves with thirty years of success and integrity!
Got my own two cents, Endmin. Erikssohn is a rickety shack, but Clavis isn't any better!
Wait. Why are you cutting in like that?
Think about it, Endministrator. A deal with a small company is like making a bet. But a deal with a giant is a swim in deep waters. Maybe Clavis is just baiting you into a bigger scheme.

Ahem. That's just my personal take on this. But should you restart the bidding process, do give me a call! I represent Mendez Manufacturing. We also took part in the last bidding, remember? It's always better to have more options, right?

options: Tell me more about your two cents, Hans.
Let the man speak.

r: Tell me more about your two cents, Hans.

lines.text: What's this...? Oh. Thank you. This is the document holder for the contract. I didn't expect it to show up here...
I was rushing to sign a contract with your company and ran into a ... minor hiccup along the way. So, I dealt with the less essential items on my own.
What do you think, Endmin?
Alright... We'll update the files today and discuss this tomorrow. I'll tell the agents of our potential partners to come back then.

options: I can't really decide right now.
I'm thinking what's for dinner.
